questions.subject: Trees
questions.question: Explain the difference between BFS traversal and Morris traversal in Trees.
questions.ideal_answer: BFS traversal and Morris traversal differ in several ways: BFS traversal is level-order traversal (works by queue-based breadth-first) whereas Morris traversal is O(1) space traversal (works by threaded binary tree technique). BFS traversal is typically used for O(n) time, O(w) space where w is max width, while Morris traversal is used for temporary links to predecessor. Example demonstrating BFS traversal: queue.offer(root); while (!queue.isEmpty()) { Node curr = queue.poll(); process(curr); queue.offer(curr.left); queue.offer(curr.right); }. Example demonstrating Morris traversal: if (curr.left == null) { visit(curr); curr = curr.right; } else { Node pred = findPredecessor(curr); if (pred.right == null) { pred.right = curr; curr = curr.left; } else { pred.right = null; visit(curr); curr = curr.right; } }.
